def-hh-right-right-hopf-module-and-coinv: The Definition imposes right action associativity/unit, coaction coassociativity/counit and the compatibility rho(mh); its coinvariants are the equality locus rho(m)=m tensor1. It defines a structure, not an equivalence theorem.
lem-hh-coinvariants-form-a-subspace: The Statement asserts only that the coinvariant equality locus is a subspace. Proof1.1 identifies it with the kernel of the linear map T(m)=rho(m)-m tensor1;2.1 proves linear closure and T(0)=0.
lem-hh-free-right-right-hopf-module: The Statement constructs the action on the H factor of V tensor H for arbitrary V. Proof1.1 checks the unit and associativity;1.2 checks coproduct coaction;2.1 and3.1 prove compatibility by multiplicativity and spanning.
lem-hh-hopf-module-coinvariant-projectio: The Statement defines P by action after the antipode on the coaction. Proof1.1 proves linearity,2.1 proves rho(P(m))=P(m) tensor1, and3.1 proves P fixes coinvariants and is idempotent without inverse antipode.
thm-hh-fundamental-theorem-of-hopf-modul: The Statement provides alpha(n tensor h)=nh and beta=(P tensor id)rho as inverse Hopf-module maps. Proof1.3 and2.1 establish both inverse identities;2.2 and3.1 establish preservation of action/coaction. These are explicit isomorphism conclusions.
lem-hh-coinvariants-of-free-hopf-module: The Statement identifies free-module coinvariants with v tensor1. Proof1.1 proves i lands in coinvariants and qi=id;2.1 uses the counit to prove iq=id on coinvariants, with no basis selection.
cor-hh-hopf-module-functor-equivalence: The Statement asserts inverse equivalences via coinvariants and the free functor. Proof1.1 and1.2 define functors;2.1 proves naturality;3.1 and4.1 calculate the two triangle identities explicitly.
ex-hh-regular-hopf-module-projection: The Example fixes the regular Hopf module H itself. Verification1.1 establishes compatibility and2.1 identifies the coinvariants k1 and projection epsilon(h)1 by the counit and antipode equations.
ex-hh-free-hopf-module-over-group-algebr: The Example allows any group G and vector space V. Verification1.2 uses canonical coefficient extractors to identify support only at the group identity;3.1 gives P(v tensor g)=v tensor e and inverse decomposition on each finite sum.
ex-hh-free-hopf-module-over-polynomial-h: The Example has the primitive polynomial Hopf structure in every characteristic. Verification2.1 gives the binomial antipode calculation;4.2 distinguishes degree n=0 from n>0;5.1 computes the inverse decomposition by its surviving i=0 term.
cex-hh-separate-action-and-coaction-fail: The fixed counterexample uses C2 and a one-dimensional space with a nonzero generator m, trivial action and coaction m tensor g. Proof2.1 contrasts m tensor g with m tensor1; a zero space would not witness this failure.
def-hh-frobenius-functional-and-associat: The Definition tests nondegeneracy by both induced maps A to A* being isomorphisms, and calls a functional Frobenius when lambda(ab) passes this test. Its final existential sentence defines Frobenius algebras; it does not prove a classification implication.
def-hh-left-right-integrals-and-integral: The Definition specifies left/right integral subspaces by equations against every algebra element and explicitly admits the zero vector. Functional equations use finite-dimensional dual convolution. It explicitly separates definitions from existence of nonzero integrals.
lem-hh-finite-dual-regular-hopf-module-c: The Statement defines the dual regular action f(xS(h)) and uniquely represented coaction by pairing. Proof1.1 uses finite tensor duality,1.2 checks compatibility,2.1 checks coaction identities, and3.1 identifies coinvariants exactly with left integral functionals.
thm-hh-hopf-maschke-integral-averaging: The Statement is an actual iff between semisimplicity and an integral with nonzero counit. Proof2.1 normalizes the augmentation splitting;1.2 and2.2 average projections;3.1 concludes semisimplicity. Existing checked implication rows are retained.
thm-hh-finite-integrals-are-one-dimensio: The Statement assumes a nonzero finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. Proof1.1 divides by its positive dimension to determine an integral dimension;1.2 and2.1 establish antipode injectivity and finite-dimensional bijectivity;3.1 transports left to right integrals.
thm-hh-finite-hopf-algebras-are-frobeniu: The Statement requires a nonzero finite Hopf algebra and nonzero integral functional, concludes isomorphism and gives two dual-basis expansions. Proof1.1 obtains the pairing isomorphism;2.1 constructs the uniquely paired finite basis;3.1 proves both-variable nondegeneracy and associativity.
ex-hh-sweedler-frobenius-pairing: The Example fixes Sweedler dimension four and characteristic different from two. Verification1.1 computes the matrix with antidiagonal entries1,1,-1,1;2.1 uses its invertibility and3.1 concludes Frobenius. It asserts a particular form, not a converse characterization.
ex-hh-finite-group-algebra-integrals-and: The Example ranges over finite groups and both characteristic regimes. Verification1.1 constructs the full group sum,2.1 compares coefficients to obtain all integrals, and3.1 evaluates its counit and applies Hopf-Maschke in both directions.
ex-hh-taft-integrals-and-maschke-failure: The Example assumes N>1, a primitive Nth root and characteristic not dividing N. lem-hh-tensor-algebra-regular-detection: The Statement restricts tensor powers to two and three. Proof1.1 constructs componentwise units;2.1 evaluates left multiplication at that unit to recover X,Y and also verifies the converse equality by substitution.
def-hh-leg-notation-and-quasitriangular-: The Definition fixes three leg insertions into left-associated triple tensors and imposes invertible algebraic R, intertwining and two leg hexagons. Verification1.1 constructs linear insertions,2.1 checks their unit products,3.1 checks involutive flip and reassociation.
lem-hh-quasitriangular-counit-and-yang-b: The Statement assumes invertible quasitriangular R. Proof1.1 and1.2 cancel R after the two counit contractions to get unit normalizations;2.1 obtains QYBE from intertwining and the first leg hexagon. The conclusion has no asserted converse.
def-hh-braiding-and-triangular-structure: The Definition uses all left modules and natural isomorphisms indexed by their pairs with two hexagons. The indexing category contains H and the zero module, so the family cannot be empty. Triangular and symmetric are defined properties; no equivalence between them is proved in this definition.
thm-hh-r-matrix-constructs-a-module-brai: The Statement includes both all-module R/braiding reconstruction and symmetric exactly when triangular. Proof2.6 proves triangular implies symmetric;4.1 evaluates on regular modules to prove the reverse. Proof1.2 and2.7 reconstruct algebraic invertible R without finite dimensionality.
lem-hh-local-braiding-operators-obey-bra: The Statement ranges over n>=2 and adjacent tensor positions. Proof1.1 proves the three-factor relation;2.1 inserts identities;3.1 checks disjoint factors. For n=2 no adjacent-triple or distant-pair constraint exists, while the sole T1 remains defined.
ex-hh-trivial-r-matrix-for-cocommutative: The Example fixes the two-dimensional C2 group algebra and R=1 tensor1 in any characteristic. Verification1.1 and2.1 establish Hopf structure and cocommutativity;3.1 verifies invertibility/legs and4.1 directly verifies the flip braiding.
ex-hh-yang-baxter-alone-does-not-give-qu: The Example fixes H=Q and R=2. Verification1.1 verifies the one-dimensional Hopf maps;1.2 gives inverse1/2 and QYBE coefficient8;1.3 distinguishes first-hexagon coefficients2 and4. It demonstrates failure of sufficiency.
ex-hh-canonical-r-matrix-for-the-double-: The Example fixes four vectors p_x#u_g indexed by C2 squared. Verification1.1,2.1,3.1 proves the structure on that basis;2.2 gives R squared equal to1;3.2 and4.1 verify intertwining and both hexagons independently of the general double theorem.
def-hh-left-left-yetter-drinfeld-module: The Definition combines unital left action, counital left coaction and the left-left compatibility equation. Proof1.1 uses coassociativity to show evaluation reverses convolution;1.2 checks the epsilon unit. No equivalence theorem is stated there.
def-hh-finite-double-cross-relations: The Definition requires finite-dimensional H and bijective S, fixes ordinary dual coproduct with opposite convolution product and defines the crossing/product bilinearly. lem-hh-double-crossing-map-and-associati: The Statement asserts unital distributive crossing laws, associativity and injective factor embeddings. Proof1.2 calculates unit crossings;1.3 and1.4 prove the two multiplication laws;2.1 compares associations and3.1 recovers factor inputs by counits.
lem-hh-double-coalgebra-and-antipode-des: The Statement provides tensor coalgebra and inverse-crossing formulas and a double antipode using S inverse. Proof1.1 establishes coassociativity;1.3 and1.4 prove mixed/general multiplicativity;1.8 computes both antipode contractions. These are construction conclusions.
thm-hh-double-modules-and-yetter-drinfel: The Statement asserts inverse module/Yetter-Drinfeld equivalences with tensor compatibility and braiding. Proof1.1 reconstructs by finite dual bases;2.4 proves inverse functors;3.2 gives inverse braiding and3.3–3.5 prove linearity/naturality/hexagons. Existing equivalence rows remain checked.
thm-hh-finite-double-hopf-structure-and-: The Statement supplies a finite canonical dual-basis tensor and explicit S-inverse tensor. ex-drinfeld-double-of-a-finite-group: The Example supplies point-mass/group basis formulas for every finite group, then identifies grading, conjugation and braiding. Its trivial-group specialization has one unit vector; no equivalence criterion with a reverse implication is asserted.
ex-a-nonabelian-double-has-noncommutativ: The Example fixes p=(12),q=(23),r=(13) in S3 and contrasts two products and the image of a basis tensor under the conjugation braiding. The witness uses distinct group basis vectors and makes no variable group-order or iff assertion.
cex-full-dual-of-infinite-group-algebra-: The refuted Statement universally proposes an algebraic coproduct on full duals. Its counterexample uses an infinite group and the identity point mass; infinitely many independent point-mass rows contradict finite tensor rank. It refutes a universal claim instead of supplying a converse.
def-hh-parabolic-hecke-subalgebra-and-in: The Definition fixes J subset S, a candidate span indexed by W_J and induction as a balanced tensor with left actions. It allows J empty and J=S; well-defined module actions are checked by balancing, with the embedding discharged separately.
def-hh-canonical-hecke-trace-and-symmetr: The Definition fixes finite W and defines tau as the coefficient at the identity standard-basis vector. Symmetry/perfectness are defined properties and proved in the justifier; a finite group W always has its identity index.
thm-hh-parabolic-hecke-freeness-and-indu: The Statement allows arbitrary W and J and an empty basis when M=0. Proof1.2–1.3 uses unique minimal representatives;2.2 gives a direct-sum induction isomorphism;3.1 proves the explicit adjunction;4.1 explains no representative choice is required.
thm-hh-canonical-hecke-trace-is-symmetri: The Statement fixes finite W but permits every commutative base change. Proof3.1 derives the inverse-index permutation pairing;4.1 gives coordinate duality;5.1 retains the same permutation matrix after base change, without assuming semisimplicity.
ex-hh-parabolic-induction-from-rank-one-: The Example fixes S3, J={s1}, Laurent parameter v and a rank-one inducing module. Verification1.1 lists all representatives,1.2 calculates six generator images,2.1 checks quadratic blocks and3.1 checks the braid matrices on the three basis vectors.
ex-hh-dual-trace-basis-in-type-a2-hecke-: The Example fixes the six S3 standard vectors over the Laurent ring. Verification2.1 gives the inverse-index permutation Gram matrix;3.1 gives its dual vectors;4.1 distinguishes trace dual T1 from algebra inverse T1-a using nonzero a.
cex-hh-perfect-symmetrizing-trace-does-n: The counterexample fixes v=i over C, so epsilon=T-i is nonzero with square zero. Step1.1 gives identity Gram matrix;1.2 proves C epsilon is the only simple submodule;2.1 shows their sum is proper, refuting the semisimplicity implication.
